About Grand Slam Fishing Charters

As a family owned business we came from fishing just for our family and friends, now we take anyone that comes close to us. From being a working man’s angler to catching the species of your dreams we will catch you a lifetime memory. We do our best to get to know every guest so the service is top not. We specialize in blue water species like Yellowfin Tuna and Silver Tuna, Wahoo, Marlin, Bigeye Tuna along with Billfish tournaments from Newport Ca to San Clemente Ca.

An experience unlike no other, my name is Aaron, a fishing guide and owner of Grand Slam Fishing Charters. Coming from a family of fisherman I always had the satisfaction of fishing with my friends and family from a very young age. Now we have a more sophisticated approach to fishing for family and friends from a business point of view and also sharing great fishing time with new comers. When you are at our shop we have a warm reception awaited for you and will make you feel right at home and if someone knows anything about fishing it’s a family member, there’s is many experiences between my family when it comes to a fishing experience and we have some great ones to share. Grand Slam Fishing Charters have many goals and the top of that list is to share quality time and quality catch with you all. The way we do it is to use the most up to date fishing techniques and equipment to satisfy every fisherman out there. With the help of family and friends we have always made sure we are doing what we love and sharing our experiences together, now looking back I see how important and the biggest key to me is the family dynamic. There’s nothing better than catching your family a lifetime memory to tell others about! We are also fully insured for you peace of mind and everyone safety for Trip Cancellation insurance so there is no denying on any day that you feel off your game there is nothing to worry about.

Grand Slam Fishing Charters is located in Huntington Beach Ca and our office is away from a residential area so incase we use our boat our office is off limits to Guests at the moment. We are still working on a local, 8 for instance, that is being built now, that we will use in the near future, details on this location will be posted on our page in the near future.

What makes Grand Slam Fishing Charters unique?
We are different than other charter fishing boats because we like to keep things traditional and we like to introduce people to what fishing was really a sport was back in the day. Our charter business is built of company’s that knew about traditional fishing and all the skills that comes with it and we are looking to carry that torch forward for many years to come. We like to expand our fishing experiences as time passes and we have lots of plans on what to do in the near future to come.

We like to do fishing but also we the family do stuff together on our days off here is a great family example. If anyone asked me what makes me different it would be the fact that I was apart of a big family when I was young. The entire family that I come from had fishing as one way to have fun and for me the best way to enjoy life with you loved ones no matter what. Fishing also has a therapeutic effect for those of us that enjoy it. Fishing for me is therapy and it has a lot of positives to it especially when it brings a great life lesson. Every year it seems that I was given a special fishing challenge and it opens peoples eyes to seeing things differently, you know you’ve caught a Great fish when it makes you catch the Great one. The catching of the Great fish is not always about the fight but the moment of that catch is truly when everything comes together!

PCI Alternative Using Sustained Exercise (PAUSE): Rationale and trial results

Abstract

Objectives To examine the efficacy of sustained high intensity exercise as an antihypertensive therapy in healthy adults.

Background Recent studies of regular exercise has shown a modest anti hypertensive effect by lowering blood pressure (BP). In addition, it also improves insulin sensitivity.1 In type- 2 diabetes a critical role of exercise is also recognized for glucose homeostasis.

However, the limitations of the training program have limited this practice for clinical applications. Currently, hypertension remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. However, 50% have uncontrolled hypertension despite optimal treatments.2

There is also growing evidence that a high energy expenditure intervention by restoring physiological responses of the cardiovascular system would be a simple strategy to restore blood pressure variability and lower daytime systolic blood pressure. Sustained high intensity exercise (PAUSE) involves high-intensity, low volume swimming exercise and performs without a progressive increase in volume. A study of the PPAUSE treatment program in 3 months showed a reduction of 20% in high-pressure (> 90 mmHg).3

There are clinical studies, however, not available to support an alternative in high and low intensity training. The scope of the study is to test the principle of low volume sustained highintensity exercise for antihypertensive effect in healthy sedentary adults.

Hypothesis Patients undergoing PaUSE protocol for high blood pressure has shown to have a reduction in blood pressure.

Methodology Subjects aged between 30 and 40years with, BMI between 20kg/m2-35kg/ m2 and not undergoing any form of drug medication were selected. The PaUSE protocol was adjusted for the subjects to complete the training schedule. At the end of the first 3-weeks of protocol, all subjects underwent resting BP with and without exercise by using the Brinkman column type tonometer. During the follow up, the trained subjects were under 3-session-a-week and non-consecutive training interval.

The data on resting and ambulatory BP during training was analyzed for significance by correlation and ANOVA. The changes of blood pressure during treatment was further defined by Wilcoxon-Sign Rank test and the changes between pre and post PPAUSE were defined by a paired t test. The data was standardized to 97% confidence interval with 10% level error.

Study Design This study was a non inter- cohort design study, however randomized or blinded method was not used during the treatment of subjects who undergo PaUSE protocol. Thirty healthy volunteers were selected for study, out of the 30 subjects 18 (78%) completed the study, subjects were selected purposively to represent the different population in our community (male 10, female 8) with age range 30 to 39years.16 of them were smokers and 1.82 kg/ m2. 4 subjects out of the 30 selected were discarded due to some pre-existing pathology.

The paUse protocol was initiated with a standardized duration of 40 minutes three times a week. 10 subjects employed more than 50minute duration during three sessions per week. These subjects who trained for more the specific application of a PaUSE duration 40 minutes have been considered to be in a protocol group and 12 subjects were selected from the control group. The control group continued with t heir routine fitness training. A comparative analysis of the pressure dynamics shows systolic and diastolic BP to be significantly different for the trainets VZ the control group with P < 0.01 (PaUse v5 control group). Systolic and diastolic blood pressure of trained subjects during exercise and after PaUSE protocol were similar. No significant difference was found between pre and post training BP.

The present result clearly depicts that a short session of sustained high-intensity exercise (PAU SE) reduces blood pressure. A possible mechanism of PAU SE

Sustained high intensive exercise of 10 minutes (PAU SE) has been postulated to reduce BP in short term. The present study is a single center case series study. The study population is small number as in the present protocol 18 of 30 patients enrolled successfully. However, the data suggests that sustained high intensity swimming reduces BP in short term. A controlled study in a larger population. needs a rigorous follow-up for a prolonged study.

I've learned the nitrogen vacancies used in Memristors behave differently than LC RAM RAM diodes in the sense that when a negative current is applied to them the resistance goes up rather than down like before. The negative current doesn't stick to one side or the other, it can act on either with equal ease.

I've seen experiments in which silicon RAM RAM diodes were replaced with nitrogen vacancies in silicon. The results were very interesting and surprising. I've believed these diodes could potentially work in high cascadeability with little degradation.

I've also had some slides on Memristive devices. Here is the slide deck page. The slides are where I've documented the developments, including the research I did on Memristor capacitors. I've also gone over how they work and what the future may hold for them. https://nsfw.org/files/memristor7/

Now, here is my first experiment with the nitrogen vacancies used in Memristors. I've read somewhere that the NVs behave like negative transistors and that the resistance seems to increase when they are oxidized through out a high positive current cycle. This is what I've seen. I did not find that when current flowed it was stronger or more effective to use oxidation to increase resistance. I thought I might find that in here too. Unfortunately that was not the case. 3. The NVM is made with doped devices. The devices are used to store information such as addresses and memory blocks, or program status. The device performs logic operations with an instruction cell and intermediate cell. Write operations are fast and require a few nanoseconds. Read operations are slow and require about 100 microseconds read cycles or longer.

  This is the best way to compare the programming of memory to the writing of a pixel.

  When the first writing occurs, the NVM is programmed with an address that will be used during the programming cycle later. The address is a number that represents the desired output value. The procedure also includes writing additional information to a memory area that contains a description of the desired output value not derived from the NVM.

  The output voltage of the device will be equal to the maximum value for which the output voltage set is defined and the input voltage will be equal to the input power supply voltage.

  After the write cycle has been completed, the output programming procedure consists of writing data in a form defined by the user, that will be used by the NVM with the address supplied by the user. The user data is written in the S-curve and is stored in the VRAM. The VRAM is a data structure of the NVM and is used for storing one or more vector control operations.
